items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: I was offered a job to work in a Road House by a fellow named Wesley Helvey and as it was an every night affair I accepted to join him.

ctx.x: After one month I got homesick for Cincinnati so I left Broadus, came home and rejoined Clarence Page. Madelyn and I were seeing each other every night and I was happy to be home with my mother and sister. My brother was still staying with my father and I went to see them often.

Page was not getting much work when I was offered a job to work in a Road House by a fellow named Wesley Helvey and as it was an every night affair I accepted to join him. I may have been lazy about doing other work but once I had gotten to the point where I could play something on my trumpet, I wanted to play as often as possible. I may have been late going to school at times or late getting to another kind of job, but I was never late when it came time to blow my horn.

Helvey also engaged Edgar Courance, who was now playing tenor sax, and a trombone player that had not been in Cincy very long. I don't remember his name except that he was called Pluto. There was a special water sold in drug stores at that time called Pluto water. Maybe this young fellow drank it and got the nickname in that manner.
